plain_title: Sleep apnoea and breathing problems in sleep
one_liner: Breathing that repeatedly stops, pauses, or becomes too shallow during sleep, breaking sleep and causing daytime exhaustion.
in_simple_words: In obstructive sleep apnoea, the airway narrows or closes during sleep, so breathing stops for seconds at a time, many times an hour, and the brain briefly wakes to restart it. People rarely remember, but they wake unrefreshed, snore loudly, and feel exhausted and foggy by day. Untreated, it raises blood pressure, heart, and accident risk. Central sleep apnoea and hypoventilation are rarer forms where the brain's breathing drive is the issue. All are very treatable.
what_it_can_feel_like: My partner said I stopped breathing in the night. I thought she was exaggerating.
I fell asleep at a red light. That's when I finally went to the doctor.
The CPAP machine took a few weeks to get used to. Now I can't believe how I used to feel.
common_signs: Loud snoring, gasping, or choking in sleep, often noticed by someone else
Waking unrefreshed, with a dry mouth or headache
Severe daytime sleepiness, falling asleep when sitting still
High blood pressure, or waking to pass urine at night

myths_vs_facts.myth: Only overweight older men get sleep apnoea.
myths_vs_facts.fact: It's more common with weight and age, but it affects women, slim people, and children too, and is under-diagnosed in women.
Loud snoring with pauses or gasping is a warning sign. Untreated apnoea raises heart and stroke risk.
Modern machines are quiet and masks come in many styles. Most people adapt within weeks and feel dramatically better.

how_common.plain: Obstructive sleep apnoea is common: estimates range from a few percent of adults to one in five or more, depending on how it's measured. Most people with it don't know.
how_common.figure: About 2%–15% of middle-aged adults (DSM-5-TR text); up to around 18% in some population estimates

what_helps.plain_summary: A sleep study (often done at home) confirms the diagnosis. For obstructive apnoea, CPAP, a machine that gently keeps the airway open with air pressure, is the main treatment and works very well. Alternatives include dental devices, positional therapy, weight management, and sometimes surgery. Central apnoea and hypoventilation need specialist assessment and different breathing support. Treating apnoea often lifts mood, blood pressure, and energy.
evidence_based_options: CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnoea
Oral appliances, positional therapy, and weight management where appropriate
Specialist breathing support for central apnoea and hypoventilation
self_help_that_supports_care: Asking a bed partner about snoring and pauses
Sleeping on your side; avoiding alcohol and sedatives before bed
Sticking with CPAP through the adjustment period and asking for a different mask if needed

when_to_reach_out: If you snore loudly, stop breathing in sleep, or are very sleepy by day, ask a doctor for a sleep assessment. Don't drive if sleepy. Mention mood and memory changes too; they often improve with treatment.
is_not: Simple snoring without pauses or daytime sleepiness isn't a disorder, though it's worth mentioning. Insomnia and narcolepsy cause sleep problems by different mechanisms.
hope_note: Treating sleep apnoea is one of the biggest quality-of-life improvements in medicine. People describe waking up for the first time in years.

in_young_people: Children with sleep apnoea often have large tonsils, snore, breathe through the mouth, and show it as hyperactivity, poor concentration, or bedwetting rather than sleepiness. Removing tonsils and adenoids is often the treatment.
across_cultures: Apnoea is under-diagnosed in women and in some ethnic groups because the 'typical patient' stereotype is a large, older man. Access to sleep studies and CPAP varies hugely by country and income.

sub_sections.title: Types
sub_sections.text: Obstructive sleep apnoea hypopnea (the airway narrows); central sleep apnoea (the brain's breathing signal pauses); sleep-related hypoventilation (breathing too shallow). Each has its own causes and treatments.
